# Dylan McDermott

> Meteorologist and geospatial data professional building weather-data workflows, maps, and operational tools.

## Profile

- Location: West Des Moines, Iowa, USA
- Current role: Meteorologist, Property & Liability Resource Bureau (January 2025-Present)
- Education: M.S. and B.S. in Meteorology, Iowa State University
- Contact: dylanddermott@gmail.com
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/dylan-mcdermott-193b18174/

## Work Examples

- [PLRB - Meteorologist](https://dylanmcd16.github.io/work/plrb-weather-systems/): Builds weather-data pipelines and claims-facing ArcGIS applications with validated catastrophe data.
- [Corteva - Research Associate](https://dylanmcd16.github.io/work/corteva-field-sensing/): Built Python and ArcPy workflows for a GPS-linked sensing platform at seven sites, saving about an hour per collection and producing plot-level summaries.
- [Master's Thesis - Iowa State University](https://dylanmcd16.github.io/work/land-use-convective-weather/): Used multi-resolution WRF and Noah-MP experiments to study how present-day and 1850 vegetation affected Midwest rainfall, surface fluxes, moisture transport, and mesoscale convective systems.
- [Iowa Severe Weather Explorer](https://dylanmcd16.github.io/projects/iowa-severe-weather-explorer/): Built an interactive replay of the August 10, 2020 Iowa derecho, combining NEXRAD, surface observations, HRRR, GOES-16, warnings, storm reports, and damage data on one timeline.

## Awards

- Esri Special Achievement in GIS (SAG) Award, 2025 - contributed to the PLRB catastrophe analytics and ArcGIS applications recognized by the award.
- AWS 10,000 AIdeas Competition Semi-Finalist - AI Weather Intelligence Platform (full-stack platform that extracts evidence and generates reports from 200+ environmental data streams).

## Core Capabilities

- Meteorology and severe weather: radar, satellite, and model interpretation; severe-weather verification and catastrophe analysis.
- Scientific research and modeling: atmospheric experiments focused on land use, Midwest rainfall, and convection; WRF, Noah-MP, CESM/LUMIP, and ERA5.
- ArcGIS and geospatial systems: ArcGIS Pro and Enterprise, ArcPy, Experience Builder, and spatial ETL.
- Coding and field data: Python, SQL, R, MATLAB, C++, REST APIs, AWS, GPS-linked instruments, LiDAR, and drone imagery.
